quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONNECTED SPEECH PHENOMENON ENUNCIATED IN THE PHRASE
quests.hint: Listen to the /t/ sound at the end of 'next' - in natural connected speech, is it fully pronounced or does it disappear? (Calibration 41-1)

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONNECTED SPEECH PHENOMENON ENUNCIATED IN THE PHRASE
quests.hint: Listen to the /n/ at the end of 'ten' - because it is followed by the velar consonant /k/, does it change to /ŋ/? (Calibration 41-2)
quests.explanation: The phrase "ten cards" demonstrates "Assimilation (/n/ changes to /ŋ/)".

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONNECTED SPEECH PHENOMENON ENUNCIATED IN THE PHRASE
quests.hint: Listen to the /t/ at the end of 'must' followed by 'be' - does it completely vanish? (Calibration 41-3)

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONNECTED SPEECH PHENOMENON ENUNCIATED IN THE PHRASE
quests.hint: Listen to the /d/ sound in 'good' - does it transform into the bilabial /b/ sound before 'boy'? (Calibration 42-1)
quests.explanation: The phrase "good boy" demonstrates "Assimilation (/d/ changes to /b/)".

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONNECTED SPEECH PHENOMENON ENUNCIATED IN THE PHRASE
quests.hint: Listen to the merging of the final /d/ in 'did' and initial /j/ in 'you' - does it sound like 'didge-you'? (Calibration 42-2)

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONNECTED SPEECH PHENOMENON ENUNCIATED IN THE PHRASE
quests.hint: In non-rhotic accents, listen to the gap between 'media' and 'event' - is a subtle /r/ sound introduced? (Calibration 42-3)

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONNECTED SPEECH PHENOMENON ENUNCIATED IN THE PHRASE
quests.hint: In non-rhotic accents, listen to the transition between 'law' and 'and' - is a subtle /r/ sound inserted? (Calibration 43-1)
